protocol.scoring: per-query CORRECT/WRONG/AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED/UNSUPPORTED/INFRA_BLOCKED; raw driver output retained (jp-raw.txt / jdt-raw.txt in longrun temp, summarized here)

javaparser.Q20_Q21_two_wildcard_ambiguity: WRONG (silently binds com.x.util.Helper / com.x.util.Runner; JLS requires ambiguity)

jdt.Q04_static_import: CORRECT (after driver set compliance=21; default source level <1.5 was a driver-config bug, not a JDT defect)
jdt.Q15_missing_dep: WRONG-unless-filtered: returns a RECOVERED binding carrying the requested FQN (org.apache.commons.math3.util.FastMath) with an explicit compile problem; integrators MUST filter ITypeBinding.isRecovered() or a phantom resolved edge is produced
jdt.Q20_Q21_two_wildcard_ambiguity: CORRECT (resolved=null + explicit 'The type Helper is ambiguous')

scip_java.evidence: official release v0.13.1 notes state 'drop Windows launcher' (PR #970); coursier native win32 launcher assets 404 across v2.1.8..v2.1.23; GitHub API rate-limited. No measurements taken; no scores inferred.

missing_dependency_degradation.jdt: recovered binding - caller must filter isRecovered()

integration_complexity.javaparser: low: subprocess + JSON, needs ambiguity-safety wrapper
integration_complexity.jdt: medium-high: dependency tree, recovered-binding filter, compliance options; best correctness
integration_complexity.scip: protobuf pipeline + build-tool integration assumptions; not measurable on Windows here

key_findings: JDT is the only measured backend with zero wrong resolutions on the gold set AND correct JLS-ambiguity refusal.
JavaParser silently violates JLS ambiguity rules (two on-demand imports) - it would reintroduce P1-class wrong bindings that the L1 resolver just fixed.
SCIP Java officially dropped its Windows launcher; on this Windows-only environment it is INFRA_BLOCKED, and its Maven/Gradle-first design conflicts with the no-build-tool degradation requirement.
L1 (tree-sitter + P1 guard) remains the only component that never fabricates ambiguity resolution; backends add recall, not safety.
